findings.body:
**Issue:** `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` previously wrapped both admin handlers; this diff registers `a.listUsers` and `a.editRoles` with no authorization middleware.

**Failure mode:** Any caller who can hit the server may `GET /api/v2/admin/users` (enumerate users) and `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` (change roles) without holding the admin role. Path prefixing under `/api/v2` does not replace access control.

**Fix:** Restore the admin role gate on these routes (per-handler wrap or subrouter `Use`):

```go
authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")
v2 := r.PathPrefix("/api/v2").Subrouter()
v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change strips admin authorization from privileged endpoints while relocating them under `/api/v2`.

## What happened

The PR moves `GET /admin/users` and `POST /admin/roles` onto a `PathPrefix("/api/v2")` subrouter. That path move is fine on its own. In the same edit, `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` is deleted and both handlers are registered as bare `http.HandlerFunc` values.

## Impact

Anyone who can reach the server can call:

- `GET /api/v2/admin/users` — user listing
- `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` — role mutation

without an admin role check. That is a privilege-escalation / broken-authorization regression on the highest-risk surface in the diff (authz + admin APIs).

## Fix direction

Keep the subrouter move, and re-wrap both handlers with `middleware.RequireRole("admin")` (or apply the same middleware on the `v2` subrouter via `Use` if that is the project pattern). Also confirm callers are updated to the new `/api/v2/admin/...` paths as part of the versioning work.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
